# Faith & Culture Campaign Framework
## Global Food Brand — Ramadan / Eid, Lunar New Year, Diwali (2026 Cycle)

*Parameter note: Islamic dates below are astronomical estimates; actual observance depends on local moon sighting and differs by country (Gulf, Morocco, Indonesia and Malaysia routinely diverge by 1–2 days). All calendar-locked media buys must carry a ±2-day flex clause. Regional naming conventions and dietary-certification claims should be re-verified with in-market counsel before creative lock.*

---

## 1. The Strategic Bet

**We have been treating cultural seasons as a creative-quality problem. They are a governance and authorship problem.**

The evidence is in our own results: the same brand, the same budget, the same season — praised in one market, accused of shallowness in another. That variance is not explained by talent. It is explained by *who wrote the work, who could stop it, and whether anyone checked what it looked like from outside the market it was made for*.

The bet: **shift from centrally-approved local execution to locally-authored work under global accountability**, with a small number of non-negotiable red lines, fast decision rights, and an explicit assumption that every asset is a global asset the moment it is published.

Three commitments follow:

1. **Authorship is local, accountability is global.** No market receives a finished idea to adapt. Markets originate; the centre governs coherence and risk, and holds veto — not authorship.
2. **Nothing is geofenced.** We plan every faith campaign as if it will be screen-recorded and posted in the market most likely to object. Because it will be, within hours.
3. **We earn the right to speak before we speak.** A brand with no year-round relationship to a community gets one-tenth the benefit of the doubt during that community's holiest month. Campaign budget without substantiation budget is a liability, not an asset.

---

## 2. Diagnosis: Why the Variance Happens

| Observed symptom | Actual root cause | Fix in this framework |
|---|---|---|
| Accurate in Gulf, tone-deaf in Southeast Asia | "Ramadan" treated as one culture; Gulf creative reskinned for Indonesia/Malaysia | Tier A pan-observance rule: shared *values* brief, market-owned *expression* |
| Praise in India, backlash from diaspora | Work optimised for domestic audience, invisible to diaspora reading it as reduction/stereotype | Diaspora Sense-Check gate (§6) |
| Factual/religious errors reaching air | Cultural review positioned as taste input after creative lock, easily overridden | External advisory with *veto*, engaged at brief stage |
| Slow, inconsistent crisis response | No pre-agreed pull authority; legal, brand and market disagree in real time | Pre-delegated pull rights + response doctrine (§8) |
| Agency quality varies by region | Roster inherited, briefs differ, no shared standard | Common Cultural Brief standard; roster qualification, not roster consolidation |

**Do not solve this by consolidating to one global agency.** That reduces variance by lowering the ceiling everywhere. Solve it by standardising *process and safeguards*, not *creative origination*.

---

## 3. Campaign Tiering

Not all seasons carry the same risk. Apply proportionate governance.

| Tier | Definition | Examples | Governance load |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A — Sacred observance** | Religious obligation; error is doctrinal, not aesthetic | Ramadan, Eid al-Fitr, Eid al-Adha, Yom Kippur | External faith advisory with veto; full gate set; no AI-generated human or script imagery; no product-hero-during-fasting-hours creative |
| **B — Religious-cultural** | Faith-rooted, widely celebrated culturally; internal diversity is high | Diwali, Christmas, Vesak, Easter | Cultural Integrity Panel with veto; full gate set; regional-variant mandate |
| **C — Cultural-civil** | Calendar/cultural celebration, contested naming or ownership | Lunar New Year / Tết / Seollal, Nowruz, Mid-Autumn | Panel advisory (escalation to veto on naming and symbol issues); market-variant mandate |

**Tier discipline:** Tier A campaigns may not use a single pan-regional master film. Tier A permits a shared *sonic and typographic system* and a shared *human truth*; food, casting, dialect, ritual and greeting are market-authored. This is the single change with the largest expected effect on our current failure rate.

---

## 4. The Authenticity Standard

Authenticity is not a feeling. Define it as four testable conditions; work that fails any one does not proceed.

| Test | Question | Evidence required |
|---|---|---|
| **Authorship** | Was the core idea originated by people who observe this season? | Named creative leads; ≥50% of the originating team observant or of the community |
| **Specificity** | Could this creative run unchanged in a different market of the same faith? | If yes → fail. Show the market-specific detail (dish, dialect, ritual, household form) |
| **Restraint** | Does the work reflect the season's actual meaning, or just its commercial peak? | Ramadan = restraint, charity, patience, family — *then* iftar. Not abundance-first |
| **Continuity** | Does the brand show up in this community outside this month? | Evidence of ≥2 non-seasonal touchpoints in trailing 12 months |

The Continuity test is the one most likely to be waived under pressure. It should not be. Seasonal-only presence is precisely the pattern that generates "shallow" accusations — the criticism is usually accurate.

---

## 5. Operating Model — Roles and Decision Rights

| Body | Composition | Mandate | Power |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Market Authorship Team** | Local marketing lead + local agency + community consultants | Originate idea, casting, food, language | Owns creative; can decline a global system that breaks locally |
| **Cultural Integrity Panel (CIP)** | Standing internal panel, 8–10, cross-market employees from relevant communities, paid time, rotating | Review at Gate 1 and Gate 3; maintain failure-mode library | Advisory (Tier C) / Veto (Tier B) |
| **External Faith Advisory** | Retained, per-tradition; scholars + practitioners, at least one per major regional interpretation | Doctrinal accuracy, symbol handling, timing | **Veto (Tier A/B)**, exercisable within SLA |
| **Diaspora Sense-Check** | Recruited panel in 4 diaspora hubs (UK, US, Canada, Gulf expat) | View work cold, outside origin context | Flag → mandatory review, not veto |
| **Global Brand Council** | CMO, Global Brand, Comms, Legal, Regional Presidents | Coherence, red lines, escalation, pull decisions | Final authority; cannot override a Tier A faith veto |

**Critical design point:** the external advisory is retained annually and briefed at *brief stage*, not shown finished films. Advisors reviewing a locked edit will either rubber-stamp it or trigger an expensive late fight. Neither is useful.

---

## 6. Approval Architecture — Five Gates

| Gate | Timing (pre-launch) | Content | Owner | SLA |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **G1 — Intent** | T-20 weeks | Season rationale, right-to-speak evidence, substantiation plan, tier assignment | Global Brand Council + CIP | 5 working days |
| **G2 — Territory** | T-14 weeks | Market-authored idea, in words. No production spend released before clearance | Faith Advisory + CIP | 7 working days |
| **G3 — Craft** | T-8 weeks | Scripts, casting, food styling, wardrobe, script/calligraphy, translation, music | Faith Advisory + market legal | 5 working days |
| **G4 — Coherence** | T-4 weeks | Cross-market read: all seasons side by side; diaspora sense-check; adjacency audit | Global Brand Comms | 3 working days |
| **G5 — Readiness** | T-1 week | Response playbook live, holding statements approved, pull authority named, listening live | Comms + Market Lead | 2 working days |

**SLA enforcement matters more than the gates themselves.** A review body that cannot answer within a week will be bypassed by the first market under deadline pressure. Fund the panels for responsiveness; if the SLA lapses without response, clearance is deemed *withheld*, not granted — and escalates to the Council same-day.

### Red Lines (no market waiver, no exceptions)

1. No Quranic verse, divine name, or scripture on packaging, disposables, promotional items or anything designed to be discarded.
2. No sacred recitation (adhan, Quranic recitation, aarti, mantras) used as background music or remixed.
3. No depiction of consumption during fasting hours in fasting-observance creative.
4. No deity imagery (Lakshmi, Ganesha and equivalents) on footwear, packaging, floor graphics or discardables.
5. No AI-generated humans, garments, hands, script or calligraphy in Tier A/B work. Human-verified script and typography only.
6. No machine-translated copy in any published asset. Native transcreation, second-native proofread, mandatory.
7. No crescent-and-star as a generic "Islam" signifier; no bindi/turban/hijab as costume shorthand.
8. No adjacency of alcohol, pork or non-certified product to faith-observance creative — including retail media placement and shelf-adjacent activation.
9. No Tier A campaign in a market where our certification (halal, vegetarian, Jain-suitable) is not fully current and auditable for every SKU featured.
10. No promotional price architecture that raises staple prices into the observance peak. This is the most common trust-destroying behaviour in the category and no campaign survives it.

---

## 7. Cross-Border Coherence: The "Everything Travels" Doctrine

Geotargeting is a media setting, not a containment strategy. Plan accordingly.

**Four coherence checks at Gate 4:**

1. **Side-by-side read.** Place all 2026 seasonal work in one room. Do Ramadan, Diwali and Lunar New Year receive comparable investment, craft and screen time? Asymmetry is the most-screenshotted evidence of insincerity.
2. **Values consistency.** Does anything we say in one market contradict a position we hold in another — on gender depiction, family structure, sourcing, or political alignment? Identify the contradiction now and choose a position, rather than discovering it in a quote-tweet.
3. **Naming register.** Confirm per-market conventions: "Lunar New Year" vs "Chinese New Year" is a live sensitivity across Vietnam, Korea and Chinese-majority markets; Tết and Seollal are distinct holidays, not translations. Ramadan is observed, Eid is celebrated — "Happy Ramadan" is a recurring own-goal. Diwali is not "the Indian Christmas."
4. **Geopolitical exposure read.** Consumer boycott dynamics affecting Western food brands in Muslim-majority markets are live and volatile. Before any Tier A investment, run a market-level read: if brand sentiment is politically contested, a high-visibility Ramadan campaign amplifies rather than repairs. In those markets, default to *substantiation without campaign* — community programmes, pricing restraint, local sourcing — and revisit paid creative the following year.

**Asset Passport.** Every published asset carries a record: originating market, advisory clearances, casting provenance, translation chain, intended and foreseeable secondary audiences, named owner. When an asset is challenged, this converts a 12-hour internal investigation into a 20-minute one.

---

## 8. Managing Live Scrutiny

### Listening
Native-language monitoring (Arabic — Gulf and Maghrebi dialects, Bahasa, Malay, Hindi, Tamil, Mandarin, Vietnamese, Turkish) with human analysts, not translation dashboards. Coverage from T-24 hours to launch +14 days, extended through the season for Tier A.

| **2. Representation critique** | Community says we were reductive or inaccurate in feel | Listen publicly, respond within 24h, commit to a process change not a platitude. Do not argue | Respond <24h |
| **3. Values/political attack** | Objection to brand's existence, ownership or geopolitics, unrelated to creative | Hold. Do not apologise for the campaign. Consistent, pre-approved position statement | Monitor; statement only if threshold crossed |
| **4. Coordinated brigading** | Inauthentic amplification, low unique-account ratio | Do not engage. Document. Platform escalation | No public response |
| **5. Internal dissent** | Employees flag discomfort | Route to CIP within 24h; treat as early warning, never as PR risk | <24h |

Do not apologise for existing, do not apologise into a Type 3 attack (it converts a political dispute into an admission), and never issue an apology that a community advisor has not read. A late, hedged, committee-written apology is worse than the original error.

**Pull authority.** Named individual per market, pre-delegated, empowered to suspend paid amplification unilaterally without Council sign-off. Suspension is reversible; 18 hours of legal debate while an asset runs is not. Full withdrawal requires Council + advisory concurrence within 12 hours.

---

| Season (est.) | Window | Markets | Tier |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Lunar New Year (Horse)** | ~17 Feb 2026 | China, SE Asia, Korea, Vietnam, diaspora | C |
| **Ramadan** | ~17/18 Feb – 19 Mar 2026 | Gulf, North Africa, Türkiye, SE Asia, diaspora | A |
| **Eid al-Fitr** | ~19/20 Mar 2026 | As above | A |
| **Eid al-Adha** | ~late May 2026 | As above | A |
| **Diwali** | ~Nov 2026 | India, SE Asia, diaspora | B |
